name: Stronger exact baselines for the fixed Many Faces strict-score search task
question: Does temporal candidate pruning remain useful when exhaustive and pruned searches share one fused native scorer, and how does it compare with fixed database-derived reference points?
inputs: Exactly the seven byte-locked input files of protocol.json; all 70,000 candidates and all 1,011 valid queries from the existing already-composited video
cpu_affinity: One available logical CPU, selected and recorded before oracle preparation; identical for all children
process_isolation: One method/order/repetition per fresh child process; serial child execution; no oracle rescoring between measured queries

method_order.rule: For block index b, add b modulo six to each base index. Each method occupies every position once across the six blocks; within-order positions are not fully balanced.

warmup: Database records at canonical indexes 0, N//2, N-1; reset the engine after all three; no measured query is a warmup

scoring.native: Fused float64 C++ scoring routine shared by exhaustive, temporal and fixed-pivot methods; Python controller and NumPy candidate masks remain
scoring.canonical_ties: Stable score then canonical candidate index
scoring.exactness_gate: Every returned top-64 ID and rank must equal the saved NumPy exhaustive oracle; all returned scores must have absolute error <=2e-12 and relative tolerance zero
scoring.native_optimality: A stronger fused baseline, not a claim that this compiler output is the fastest attainable native implementation

temporal.history: One past fully scored query; empty at each pass; same query-change bound and 60% refresh rule as v1

pivots.selection: Farthest-first traversal over unchanged engines.embedding database descriptors (371-dimensional float32), starting at canonical index N//2; squared L2 distances accumulated in float64; ties choose smallest canonical index
pivots.prefix: The eight selected pivots must be the prefix of the 32-pivot selection
pivots.score_tables: S(pivot,candidate), separately precomputed for both compensate_roll policies; never reversed
pivots.seed: Choose the pivot minimizing its saved kth score plus the current query-change bound; ties use pivot selection order; rescore that pivot's saved top-64 to obtain U
pivots.retain: Keep c if every pivot j satisfies S(p_j,c)<=U+L(q,p_j)+epsilon_j; retain all seed candidates explicitly and retain bound equality
pivots.interpretation: System configurations with different seeds and memory/build costs; candidate counts need not improve monotonically from 8 to 32

timed: conversion of returned IDs/scores to Python lists
freeze: Save protocol/source/input/oracle/native-binary hashes before performance passes; fail if any locked file changes; retain each pass and failed attempt
failure_policy: Correctness mismatch or changed locks aborts the run. Preserve the failed evidence; do not relax tolerance or silently discard a run.
interpretation: Compare native exhaustive and native temporal within this new run. Do not form speed ratios between new native timings and v1 Faiss/NumPy timings on a different host. One composited clip does not establish generalization, human similarity quality, video quality, or end-to-end application speed.
registration: Internal fixed protocol written before v2 performance measurement; not an externally registered experiment
